This petition is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 15 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., seeking to quash the proceedings pending in P.C.No.162/2022 pending on the file of learned Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Shahapur, and FIR registered in Crime No.72/2023 by Shahapur NC:
2023:KHC-K:8681 Police Station, Yadgiri District, for the offences punishable under Sections 420,
463, 464, 468 r/w Section 149 of IPC.

2 . Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.

sentences.text: Case of the complainant before the Magistrate is that the complainant said to be shareholder in Krishna Pattana Sahakaara Bank (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'Bank') and his Membership Number is 145650.
The petitioners are said to be Board of Directors and there was misappropriation of funds by the petitioners and other employees of the Bank.

Therefore, an enquiry was made by the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies and on 02.07.2022, the report was submitted to the Joint Registrar of Co-Operative Societies, Bengaluru, under Section 64 of the Karnataka Co-Operative Societies Act (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') and it was confirmed that these petitioners and other staff of the Bank were involved in misappropriation of funds and have NC:
2023:KHC-K:8681 cheated the members to the tune of Rs.616.79 lakhs.
Though the complainant approached the police for filing the complaint, the police refused to receive the complaint.
He has also sent a copy of the complaint to the Superintendent of Police, Yadgiri, through RPAD, but no action was taken.
Hence the complainant filed private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., and got it referred to Shahapur Police, for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.
In turn, the police registered FIR and submitted to the Magistrate.
During the investigation, the Police Sub-Inspector submitted report to the Magistrate for transferring the investigation to the CID as the amount of misappropriation was more than Rs.5.00 crores.
Accordingly, direction was issued and the papers were forwarded to the CID, Branch Bengaluru and the investigation has been taken up by the CID which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners strenuously contended that the complaint filed by respondent No.2 is NC: 2023:KHC-K:8681 premature and the mistake of law.

The Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies submitted report under Section 64 of the Act wherein it was found that the staff of the Bank i.e., accused Nos.16 to 19 have actually misappropriated the amount by sanctioning loan to their kith and kins against the provisions of Section 110 of the Act and there is no offence made out against the petitioners in the report.
Prior to passing final order under Section 68 of the Act, by the Joint Registrar of the Co- operative Societies, complaint came to be filed.

He further contended that the Joint Registrar found the Manager and other staff members of the Bank guilty as they have sanctioned the loan in the name of their kith and kins without bringing to the notice of the Board of Directors who are the petitioners.
Therefore, a direction was issued by the Joint Registrar to the CEO of the Bank for lodging the complaint.
Accordingly, complaint was lodged by the in-charge Manager of the Bank in PCR No.135/2023 and the same is pending before the learned Magistrate for enquiry.
Absolutely, there is no material NC: 2023:KHC-K:8681 against the petitioners for having committed the offences under Section 420 of IPC or misappropriation of funds.
He further submits that petitioner No.1 has also filed defamation case against respondent No.2/complainant for filing false complaint.
The very complaint itself is not sustainable without prior sanction.

The sanction was already issued by the Director of the Co-operative Society against accused Nos.16 to 19 and earlier Manager and therefore, prayed for quashing of the complaint against the petitioners.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 has filed statement of objections contending that the petitioners have manipulated the audit report and therefore, the earlier Manager one Channabasavanna has already filed Private Complaint in PCR No.156/2023 against the petitioners which is pending before the learned Magistrate for enquiry.
The complainant approached the Police as well as Superintendent of Police for filing compliant, but they have not taken any action.

There is misappropriation of funds amounting to Rs.616.79 lakhs pertaining to the members of the Co-operative Society.
Therefore, the matter requires investigation and accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners, I have perused the records.

8. It is not in dispute that respondent No.2 was one of the Members of the Bank and the petitioners are the Directors of the said Bank and they are arrayed as accused Nos.1 to 15 in the private complaint.
The records would indicate that respondent No.2 approached the police for filing the complaint, but they have not entertained.
Respondent No.2 has also sent a copy of the complaint to the Superintendent of Police, Yadgiri, through RPAD, but no action was taken.
Hence, the complainant has filed the private complaint.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that when there is misappropriation or embezzlement of funds of the Bank, no sanction is required under Section 111 of the Act.
Therefore, the matter is required to be investigated.

9. On hearing the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the records especially paragraphs-9 and 10 of the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8681 complaint filed by respondent No.2, it reveals that there was misappropriation of fund by the petitioners and other employees of the Bank.

Therefore, the enquiry was made by the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies and on 02.07.2022, the report was submitted to the Joint Registrar of Co-Operative Societies, Bengaluru, under Section 64 of the Act and it was confirmed that these petitioners and officials were involved in misappropriation of funds and have cheated the members of the Society to the tune of Rs.616.79 lakhs.

Based upon the said report, complaint came to be filed by respondent No.2, whereas learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the report under Section 64 of the Act is only a provisional report and there is no final order passed by the Joint Registrar of Co-operative Societies under Section 68 of the Act.
Subsequently, the learned counsel for the petitioners has also produced the order dated 21.04.2023 passed by the Joint Registrar of Co-operative Societies under Section 68 of the Act.

The audit report was the basis for filing the complaint by respondent No.2.
Whereas the report under Section 64 of the Act was submitted by the Deputy Registrar based on the audit report submitted by the Auditor of the Bank.

Based on the report submitted by the Deputy Registrar under Section 64 of the Act, the Joint Registrar passed an order under Section 68 of the Act wherein the allegation of misappropriation of funds is alleged against accused Nos.16 to 19 but not against accused Nos.1 to 15/petitioners.

10. Based on the sanction granted by the Joint Registrar, the in-charge Manager has already filed private complaint in PCR No.135/2023 against the earlier Manager and the staff members of the Bank for the offences punishable under Sections 109(12) and 109(15) of the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959 r/w Sections 403 and 409 r/w Section 34 of IPC.
The said case is pending before the learned Magistrate.

Of-course, the earlier Manager also filed complaint against the petitioners - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8681 stating that the audit report was manipulated and the same has to be considered in the said complaint and not in this case.
But, in the present case, absolutely, there is no material against the petitioners.
The petitioners are not involved in commission of offence in order to take cognizance for investigating the matter either by police or by the Higher Officials like CID or CEN Police.

If any material is found by the police during the investigation or enquiry in respect of the complaint filed by the in-charge Manager, based upon the order passed by the Joint Registrar under Section 68 of the Act, in PCR No.135/2023, then the Court can take cognizance and implead any person as additional accused.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that, absolutely, there is no case made out against the petitioners.

Such being the case,
continuation of the proceedings against the petitioners amounts to abuse of process of Court.

Hence,

Basawaraj And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47223852/
7 the FIR registered against the petitioners is required to be quashed.
Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
The proceedings in PCR No.162/2022 pending on the file of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Shahapur, and FIR registered in Crime No.72/2023 by Shahapur Police Station, Yadgiri District, for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 464, 468 r/w Section 149 of IPC insofar as the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 15 are hereby quashed.
In view of disposal of the main petition I.A.No.2/2023 filed for vacating stay does not survive for consideration.
Accordingly, the same stands disposed of.
